title: Dick Billings visits Sheehan over the sealed Iran-Contra complaint

tellings.quote: he said there aren't two men in the world that would have answered that question that way he said my name is was Dick Billings I was the chief staff writer for the house select committee on assassinations I think I can help you out on this case

plain: In the 1980s, while his Christic Institute was preparing a sealed racketeering lawsuit over the Iran-Contra affair, the lawyer Dan Sheehan says a man turned up at the institute's office at 1324 North Capitol Street in Washington and offered to help. Sheehan tells Michels the man said there "aren't two men in the world that would have answered that question that way", then introduced himself as Dick Billings, chief staff writer for the House Select Committee on Assassinations, Congress's inquiry into the Kennedy and King killings. Sheehan tells it as the start of help from someone who had seen the government's secrets up close.
